rejected_approach.reason: All three complete development workloads were slower; reopening states outweighed skipped orders. Reduced deterministic edges additionally need lazy reconstruction for policy evaluation.

reason_for_three_finalists: Keep both close Python methods and the compiled method: development shows cold-start overhead reverses the ranking on small inputs while the larger medium case benefits from compilation. Three includes the selected cold method and its closest correct rival; the third measures the user's large learning workload.
fixed_selection_rule: Among semantically correct, complete, equal-output methods, use the lowest sum of per-case median complete compute time on the three frozen medium cases. Report overlapping aggregate ranges as uncertainty. Do not replace this rule after inspecting heldout results.
scope_of_recommendation: Report cold-medium selection, heldout reversals, full-hard results, and any separately measured resident-process throughput independently. No universal fastest method is asserted; the learning API exposes reference, cache, and native choices.
isolation: Fresh child process per algorithm/case/trial, serial, alternating order; one separate one-state warmup. Reserve host during measurements. Include parsing, setup, cached JIT, enumeration, skyline, materialization, hashing and cleanup in compute; save time and complete process wall separately.
memory: Whole child lifetime OS peak resident memory in bytes, including serialization.
hard_budget: Attempt all three approaches on both full cases within the independent T2 observation budget of 120 minutes. Preserve incomplete results without ranking their prefixes.
